method: Independent ordinary visible UI play, normal http://127.0.0.1:5173/ only; visible-playtest browser synthetic input, short paused batches, fallback mouse-button drag look; installed headed Chrome with software WebGL.

used: R reload rifle and shell insertion

obstacles_and_failures: First movement hit foreground cover; Space did not clear that obstacle; strafed around.
Cabinet and shelf walls repeatedly obscured receiver approach; map and ground trace helped recover routes.
Recovery attempts at 8m, 4.5m and 3.7m failed until closer; explicit move-closer feedback was useful.
Held breacher firing missed moving Sentinel; only two shells spent in 1.5 seconds, later shell reload visibly restored 4 to 6.
Some intended rapid fallback look changes failed to rotate as expected; isolated mouse-button look plus wait worked.
Large turns and target movement caused fire into empty space, shutters or inert/occluding parts. Preserve as real misses, not evidence of broken hit detection.
Patrols accumulated while concentrating on coils. Both runs died from incoming threats; second cleared jammer but died before moving to extraction.
Second final capture began with 8 health / RETURN TO EXTRACTION and ended on death during photograph/pause; synthetic capture scheduling limits precise timing interpretation.
presentation_observations: Strong coherent teal/amber storm-industrial identity, clean title typography and wet-floor lighting.
Weapon, robot and facility geometry remain visibly simple and repetitive at close range; open grey skyline and repeated rectangular cover reduce richness.
HUD health/ammo, named objectives and numbered coil percentages are legible.
Several simultaneous messages, brackets, directional threats and center objective panels compete in close combat. Coil physical faces require circling and keeping track of which dark coil is inert.
score_basis: Playable tactical movement and recover/disable progression with useful shield/recovery feedback. Attractive coherent slice presentation, but simplified environment/actors and dense combat overlays; two ordinary deaths and no extraction coverage preclude strong completion claims. Scores are independent subjective observations under this method.
limitations: Pause-assisted synthetic input and fallback drag look limit aiming and continuous-action judgments.
No human enjoyment judgment, audio validation, physical hardware/performance benchmark or AAA certification.
No upload, victory or full extraction coverage. Exact shots and misses unavailable in visible UI; end accuracy retained without inventing counts.
Only own UI/screenshots and driver help inspected; no source/state/debug/test URL/controllers/resources inspected.
